name: VeriSign
description: VeriSign runs the authoritative registry for the .com and .net top-level domains, the database that lets a name like example.com resolve on the internet, and it also operates the root-zone maintainer function and back-end services for some other domains. It does not sell names to the public; registrars (such as GoDaddy) pay VeriSign a set wholesale fee for each annual .com or .net registration and renewal and sell the name on to the registrant. The fee is capped by contract with ICANN and the U.S. Department of Commerce, and .com can be raised up to 7 percent a year in four of every six years. Almost all revenue comes from about 173.5 million .com and .net registrations. Costs are small, so operating margin was 67.7 percent in FY2025, and cash goes to buybacks and, since Q2 2025, a quarterly dividend.

gics.note: Conventional label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source in this pass. SEC SIC code is 7371 (Computer Programming Services). The box misleads: VeriSign does not sell software or IT projects. It is a regulated registry monopoly for .com and .net whose price is set by contract with ICANN and the U.S. Department of Commerce, not by the market, and it has one reportable segment with a 67.7 percent operating margin.

hq.note: 12061 Bluemont Way, Reston, VA 20190 (FY2025 10-K); incorporated in Delaware

employees.note: 928 employees, of which 926 full-time; about 93% in the U.S. (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: .com and .net registry (single reportable segment)
businessLines.how: Registrars, its direct customers, pay a fee per annual registration or renewal (registrations run from one to ten years). Revenue moves with the number of registrations, the renewal rate and permitted price increases; the .com wholesale fee was raised from $9.59 to $10.26 effective September 1, 2024, and Verisign pays ICANN $0.2575 per annual .com registration out of it.
businessLines.description: Registry operator for .com and .net, plus a smaller set of other gTLD registries, one ccTLD (.cc) and back-end services (e.g., .edu). Verisign reports one segment; other registries are 'not significant in relation to consolidated revenues' (10-K), so no split is published.

operatingProfit.note: +6% vs FY2024; margin 67.9% FY2024 and 67.0% FY2023 (percent-of-revenue table)

brands.name: .com
brands.note: Largest registry; price capped by ICANN agreement. Split of the 173.5M .com and .net base between .com and .net not extracted

brands.name: .net
brands.note: Second registry; price cap up to 10% a year through June 30, 2029

brands.name: .name, .cc, .edu back-end, other gTLD back-end
brands.note: Not significant in relation to consolidated revenues (10-K)
